title: Climate Justice & Resilient Communities
reference_framework: IPCC AR6 synthesis; IFSW ethical principles

modules.title: Climate risk, inequity, and rights
modules.outcome: Distinguish a climate hazard from unequal exposure, vulnerability and capacity to respond.

teaching_points.text: A hazard map does not fully describe social risk: exposure, housing, livelihood dependence and capacity to respond can differ within the same area.
Do not describe communities only through deficits; identify local knowledge, mutual support and resources alongside constraints.
Displacement-related planning must consider access to livelihoods, services, relationships and meaningful participation; moving people is not itself proof of a just outcome.
Participation records should identify whose perspectives are missing, not equate attendance with representation.
Separate observed local impacts from explanations that need specialist evidence; avoid attributing every individual event to climate change without support.

modules.title: Community-led adaptation and resilient services
modules.outcome: Compare adaptation options with communities, including accessibility, maintenance and unintended consequences.

teaching_points.text: Co-design begins while choices can still change; consultation after a fixed design offers limited influence.
An adaptation option may reduce one risk while shifting burdens elsewhere; assess who benefits and who may be harmed.
Accessible services need usable routes, communication and support; a nominal facility is not enough if intended users cannot reach or use it.
Compare adaptation options over their operating life, including responsibility and resources for upkeep.
Combine appropriate technical advice with community knowledge; conflicting accounts should prompt investigation rather than automatic dismissal.

modules.title: Just transition, advocacy, and accountability
modules.outcome: Assess how climate decisions distribute benefits and burdens and propose accountable follow-up.

teaching_points.text: A transition plan should examine who loses income or access as well as who gains; affected workers and communities need a meaningful role.
An accountability route needs accessible reporting, a responsible responder and a way to track responses without exposing complainants unnecessarily.
Disaggregate benefits where appropriate and safe: an average can hide who is not being reached.
Use evidence that matches the claim and acknowledge uncertainty when communicating with decision-makers.
Review an intervention when evidence shows new burdens; record the concern, consult affected people and use the authorised adjustment process.

questions.question: Two neighbourhoods face similar flood forecasts. One has accessible transport and secure housing; the other lacks both. What should a social-risk review examine?

options.text: Only whether the forecast uses the same colour for both areas
Only which area pays more property tax
Whether all residents can be assigned an identical risk score
How living conditions and response capacity change the consequences of the hazard

questions.rationale: The same forecast can have different consequences. Social conditions and available support matter to the review.

questions.question: A climate assessment lists only residents' weaknesses. What information would improve the assessment?

options.text: An assumption that outside organisations must make every decision
Residents' existing knowledge, networks and adaptation resources
Only the value of imported equipment
A replacement list written without residents

questions.rationale: An asset-aware assessment can identify feasible locally supported actions rather than treating residents as passive recipients.

questions.question: A relocation proposal reduces flood exposure but moves families far from jobs and accessible services. What is the most useful next analysis?

options.text: The combined safety, livelihood and access effects with affected residents
Whether residents can be excluded from the final discussion
Only the number of buildings constructed
Only whether the new site is outside the mapped flood zone

questions.rationale: A single improvement does not establish the overall effect. Trade-offs need to be understood with those affected.

questions.question: A climate consultation is attended mainly by property owners, although many residents rent. What is the main evidence gap?

options.text: Proof that renters have no relevant experience
The experiences and priorities of renters and other absent groups
A lack of enough photographs of the meeting
A need to count property owners twice

questions.rationale: Attendance by one group cannot establish the views of groups that were not reached.

questions.question: A worker documents repeated heat-related disruption at a community centre. Which statement best respects the evidence available?

options.text: Remove the observation because the worker is not a climate scientist
State that this single observation proves the cause of every local heat event
Describe the observed disruption and seek relevant climate evidence before making attribution claims
Present an assumed future temperature as a measured fact

questions.rationale: The observation is useful, but stronger causal claims need additional evidence. Recording its limits preserves credibility.

questions.question: An adaptation project asks residents for views after the contractor and design are final. What would make the next planning cycle more participatory?

options.text: Invite residents only to the opening ceremony
Ask residents to endorse the existing design without changes
Involve residents before options are fixed and show how their input changes decisions
Publish a survey after all funds are spent

questions.rationale: Input has greater practical value when participants can influence meaningful choices and see the response.

questions.question: A drainage project protects a commercial area but diverts water toward lower-income homes. What is the key review question?

options.text: Whether the protected buildings look newer
Whether the budget was spent on time
Whether the project can omit the affected homes from reports
Whether the design transfers risk and what safer alternatives are available

questions.rationale: Risk reduction in one place can worsen another group's exposure. Delivery speed alone does not establish an equitable result.

questions.question: A cooling centre is free but has steps at every entrance. Which change best addresses the identified access barrier?

options.text: Work with disabled residents to provide a safe usable access route and necessary support
Require residents to provide their own lifting assistance
Count everyone in the district as already served
Advertise that admission is free more often

questions.rationale: The issue is practical access, not price alone. A usable route should be designed with the people affected.

questions.question: A donated water-storage system has no maintenance owner or budget. What should be resolved before treating it as a sustainable service?

options.text: Only which donor logo will appear on it
Who maintains it, with what resources, training and reporting arrangements
Whether the purchase price can be reported as zero
Only the installation date

questions.rationale: Installation does not guarantee continued service. Ownership and upkeep resources are part of feasibility.

questions.question: Residents report that a proposed meeting site becomes inaccessible during heavy rain, but the planning map shows no problem. What should the team do?

options.text: Investigate the discrepancy with residents and relevant technical partners
Discard every technical source immediately
Proceed and collect complaints only after launch
Reject the residents' account because it is not a map

questions.rationale: Different evidence sources may reveal different conditions. Investigating the discrepancy can improve the plan.

questions.question: A cleaner-energy programme closes a polluting facility but offers no plan for affected workers. What should a just-transition review add?

options.text: A statement that all workers will automatically find new work
A rule preventing workers from raising concerns
Worker and community participation in assessing livelihood impacts and support options
Only the project's emissions estimate

questions.rationale: Environmental benefits do not erase distributional consequences. Livelihood effects and participation need explicit attention.

questions.question: Residents can submit climate-project complaints, but nobody is assigned to respond. What is the most important missing element?

options.text: A larger complaint box with the same process
A requirement to publish every complainant's name
A limit allowing complaints only on opening day
A clear response owner and a trackable follow-up process

questions.rationale: Collecting complaints without responsibility for action does not establish an effective accountability route.

questions.question: A programme reports improved average access to water. Which further check best tests fairness?

options.text: Whether improvement reaches groups facing the greatest access barriers
Whether the report contains more project photos
Whether unsuccessful households can be excluded from the denominator
Whether the average can be rounded upward

questions.rationale: A positive average may coexist with persistent exclusion. Distribution matters alongside the headline result.

questions.question: A campaign has ten resident interviews about a local drainage issue. Which claim is best supported?

options.text: The project is guaranteed to solve all future flooding
These interviews describe concerns that warrant further local investigation
The interviews prove the exact prevalence across the country
Every resident agrees with every interviewee

questions.rationale: The interviews provide situated accounts, not a national prevalence estimate or a guarantee.

questions.question: Monitoring shows an adaptation project's fees exclude some intended users. What is the best next step?

options.text: Stop recording low-income users
Declare the exclusion unrelated without investigation
Review affordability with affected users and responsible decision-makers, then consider adjustments
Keep the fees unchanged because the launch was successful

questions.rationale: Monitoring should inform decisions. The observed barrier calls for review rather than removal from the evidence.
